discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 250554
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
154 AM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Areas of fog are possible in northwest Ohio and northeast 
  Indiana this morning.

- Dry and pleasant weather persists through the week with highs
  generally in the 70s and lows around 50.

- The next chance of widespread rain does not arrive until
  Saturday night. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 154 AM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

Yet another day where fog is the only main forecast concern. This 
morning's fog forecast is more challenging than yesterday because 
winds have veered to a more southerly direction and we lost 
good Lake Erie contribution. Still, excellent radiational 
cooling conditions exist with the loss of any upper level clouds
and some moisture appears to still be bleeding into northwest 
OH from the lake. Guidance continues to show a narrow swath of 
dense fog developing along the Maumee River with some 
observational evidence starting to support this idea. Confidence
in widespread dense fog is much lower this morning and for now 
seems to be more of a localized, SPS-level event. Will continue 
to monitor obs closely through the morning and consider a dense 
fog advisory for the Fort Wayne to Wauseon corridor if necessary.

Lack of widespread fog and some light southerly flow/WAA today 
should push highs into the low 70s for most with some mid 70s 
possible in the far SW. Afternoon RH values drop to around 35 
percent and dry fine fuels will continue to support some concern for 
small field fires (limited by very light winds). Winds veer even 
more for Monday morning and while some patchy fog may still be 
possible given light winds, not expecting any widespread/dense fog 
at this time, especially as crossover temps may be harder to exceed 
for Monday morning. A weak front washes out across our north on 
Monday and a brief return to cool NE flow arrives Tue morning. This 
will be another day to watch for possible fog development given ENE 
flow over the very warm lakes. Light S/SW flow returns Wed and Thu 
ahead of the next front and highs surge well into the 70s (possibly 
near 80 far SW). This front also washes out across our north as
parent trough lifts into Quebec and ridge holds firm over the 
Ohio Valley. A few sprinkles are possible in our far NW on Thu 
but chances are low and impacts nil. SW flow quickly recharges 
heading into Halloween with highs well into the 70s and mainly 
dry conditions. Will have to watch the next decent system 
arriving Sat night into Sunday for more widespread rain chances.
Still plenty of time for subtle changes but for now best 
chances for rain appear later Saturday night into Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 135 AM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

The western periphery of an expansive low level anticyclone
across the eastern CONUS will maintain its influence across
northern Indiana today. Weak low level flow has veered a bit
over past 12 hours with a slow eastward migration to an upper
ridge axis across central CONUS, and this will result in
continued subtle veering through this period. In the meantime,
stagnant synoptic conditions will lead to another morning of fog
potential. Veering of the flow will result in this threat not
being as widespread as yesterday morning, but TEMPO vsbys under
1 mile at KFWA in the 08Z to 12Z period still seems reasonable.
Fog is expected to remain more patchy in nature in KSBN vicinity
with lower confidence at this terminal. Weak south flow will
develop today with VFR conditions after 14Z once any AM fog
dissipates. The potential of fog appears somewhat lower tonight
with continued veering of low level wind profiles and less
influence from eastern Great Lakes.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...Marsili

spc.summary: Isolated large hail, and a tornado or two will be possible this afternoon/evening across central/eastern New Mexico and Far West Texas. An isolated damaging wind gust will also be possible across Far West Texas.
spc.text:
SPC AC 250555

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1255 AM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
   OF CENTRAL AND EASTERN NEW MEXICO AND FAR WEST TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated large hail, and a tornado or two will be possible this
   afternoon/evening across central/eastern New Mexico and Far West
   Texas. An isolated damaging wind gust will also be possible across
   Far West Texas.

   ... Southern and Eastern New Mexico into Far West Texas ...

   A midlevel shortwave trough is expected to eject northeastward
   across the Four Corners region ahead of stronger height falls
   approaching the Pacific Northwest. Although this trough should
   gradually weaken, associated large-scale ascent will overspread the
   northwestern periphery of a persistent low- to midlevel moist plume
   extending across New Mexico. A slow-moving, northeast to
   southwest-oriented baroclinic zone will provide a focus for
   convective development, with differential heating and
   terrain-induced vertical circulations likely contributing to
   thunderstorm initiation during the afternoon. 

   The thermodynamic environment across the region will be somewhat
   complex. Steeper midlevel lapse rates will generally reside
   northwest of the surface warm sector, closer to the ejecting
   shortwave trough, while the richer low-level moisture will remain
   displaced farther southeast. Additionally, repeated convective
   episodes over the preceding several days have acted to temper lapse
   rates across portions of the warm sector. This, combined with
   potentially extensive cloud cover, should limit the magnitude and
   spatial extent of destabilization.

   That said, surface dewpoints in the middle 50Fs to near 60F should
   support pockets of MLCAPE approaching 1000 J/kg where sufficient
   insolation occurs. This degree of buoyancy may prove sufficient for
   sustained deep convection. Given forecast wind fields across the
   region indicative of deep-layer shear between 35-40 knots, the
   CAPE-shear parameter space will support supercells capable of large
   hail, generally in the 1-1.5 inch range. Additionally, forecast
   hodographs suggest enough low-level curvature to support a tornado
   or two with any sustained, discrete supercell. 

   Despite the seemingly favorable ingredients within the large-scale
   environment, the severe weather threat should remain somewhat
   conditional. Questions remains surrounding both the degree and
   spatial extent of instability, and subsequently the spatial overlap
   of favorable thermodynamics and kinematic fields. This uncertainty
   limits confidence in a more substantial severe threat.  That said, a
   more focused corridor or two of higher severe potential could become
   apparent later today as mesoscale details and convective evolution
   become better resolved. 


   ... Oregon Coast ...

   Isolated thunderstorms may occur near the Oregon coast early on
   Sunday as the cold core of an approaching midlevel trough moves into
   the area. Shallow convective cells may become sufficiently deep to
   produce sporadic lightning. 


   ... Southeast Florida ...

   Across southeast Florida, moist northeasterly flow along the western
   periphery of a midlevel low over the Bahamas may support occasional
   thunderstorms. Weak forecast vertical shear and warm mid-level
   temperatures should limit any organized severe potential.

   ..Marsh/Thornton.. 10/25/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 250502

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1202 AM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential is expected to be low on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...

   An upper shortwave trough initially over the southern/central High
   Plains, will lift northeast to the Upper Midwest on Monday into
   early Tuesday. Large-scale upper troughing will persist across the
   western U.S. as a deepening cyclone and attendant shortwave trough
   deepen and spread southeast over the Great Basin and Intermountain
   West. Southerly low-level flow will maintain modest boundary layer
   moisture across the southern Plains vicinity ahead of a cold front
   progressing south/southeast across the central Plains and Mid-MO
   Valley. 

   Modest destabilization is forecast from southwest TX,
   southern/eastern NM, portions of the OK/TX Panhandles, and far
   southwest KS. Isolated thunderstorms may develop toward late
   afternoon through evening. Effective shear around 25-30 kt could
   support transient storm organization, but southwest flow below 500
   mb is forecast to remain fairly weak. Furthermore, warmer midlevel
   temperatures may hinder stronger updrafts despite modest
   instability. While the strongest storms could produce small hail,
   overall severe potential appears limited, precluding Level
   1/Marginal risk probabilities.

   ..Leitman.. 10/25/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 250639

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0139 AM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A series of upper troughs will migrate across the north-central U.S.
   on Tuesday while upper ridging amplifies over the East. Southerly
   low-level flow will maintain modest boundary layer moisture (mainly
   50s F dewpoints) from OK/KS into the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes, with
   60s F dewpoints possible further south across TX. A surface front
   initially over KS to central IA will lift northward through the
   period in response to increasing low-level warm advection ahead of a
   shortwave trough traversing the northern Plains. Isolated
   thunderstorms are possible within the broader warm advection regime
   across parts of the Plains from South TX into the Mid-MO Valley.
   Modest instability and generally weak vertical shear will preclude
   severe potential.

   ..Leitman.. 10/25/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
